target_definition: Discharge capacity divided by this battery's first positive measured discharge capacity, multiplied by 100.
interpretation: Operational capacity-retention research proxy; not certified physical or personalized battery SoH.

split.test_warmup: First 19 discharge observations omitted to match sequence models' 20-observation history eligibility.

experiments.architecture: Simple linear degradation trend fitted on training cells (B0005, B0018)
Gradient-boosted decision trees on cycle index (models/nasa_first_positive_retention_xgboost.json)
2-Layer Recurrent LSTM with 20-cycle chronological sequence window (models/nasa_first_positive_retention_lstm.pt)
2-Layer Gated Recurrent Unit with 20-cycle chronological sequence window (models/nasa_first_positive_retention_gru.pt)
Constant training-set target mean (91.13% capacity retention)

limitations: The target is each NASA battery's capacity divided by its own first positive measured capacity; it is an operational proxy, not a certified physical SoH reference.
Evaluation has one unseen test battery (B0006), with 149 scored observations after sequence warmup.
On the held-out test battery, the simple linear cycle-trend baseline achieved lower RMSE (7.073 pp vs 8.481 pp) and higher R² (0.559 vs 0.365) than XGBoost.

Deep sequence models (LSTM, CNN-LSTM, GRU) exhibited negative R² on unseen cell B0006 due to cross-cell distribution shifts, demonstrating that sequence models trained on few cells do not automatically generalize to new cells without calibration.
NASA README and battery-specific discharge protocol cutoff descriptions differ; this model predicts dataset-level capacity degradation from cycle history only.
